title: fadd: drop the s2 exponent pre-increment and the s3 zero detector (both are redundant)
hypothesis:
# fadd: drop the s2 exponent pre-increment and the s3 zero detector (both are redundant)

Category: area

## Motivation

otpu_fadd is 64 x (317 LUT + 181 FF) = 20288 LUT + 11584 FF, 75% of the unit's area_eq (42290).
Each LUT removed from it is worth 64 area_eq, and each FF 32. The -1% gate is 423 area_eq, so
about 7 fadd LUTs.

The fadd pipe computes two things it does not need:

1. **s2's `q.e = r.e + 8'd1`** is an 8-bit incrementer (about 8 LUTs, bit 7 depends on all 8
   inputs) that exists only to pre-bias the exponent for s3's 28-bit normalize
   (`n.e = q.e - n`). The +1 is a constant. It can move into s4's constant comparisons and into
   the exponent adder s4 already has (`8'(e0) + 8'(c)`), where it costs nothing.
2. **s3's cancellation test `q.sum == 0`** is a 28-input NOR (5 or 6 LUTs in two levels) on
   `s2.sum`. `s2.sum` is the high-fanout source of every worst fadd path
   (`s2_reg[sum][20]` -> s3.e / s3.mn, 3.02 to 3.4 ns slack). norm28 already computes this bit:
   its five shift stages move any nonzero 28-bit value all the way up (16+8+4+2+1 = 31 >= 27), so
   `nz.y[27] == (q.sum != 0)` exactly. After norm28's last stage,
   `nz.y[27] = y4[27] | y4[26]`, which is the same LUT level as `mn[26]`.

The s3 exponent also carries one bit too many. `n.e` is declared `signed [9:0]`, but its range is
[-31, 255], which fits in 9 signed bits. That is one FF plus the top-bit logic of the s3 subtract
and the s4 compares.

## Change (rtl/vpu/otpu_fp.sv only; otpu_fpipe.sv unchanged)

- `fadd_p2_t.e`: now the larger operand's exponent, **not** incremented. Update the comment.
- `fp_add_s2`: `q.e = r.e;` (delete the `+ 8'd1`).
- `fadd_nm_t.e`: `logic signed [8:0] e;`. It holds `x = e_larger - n`, which is **one less** than
  today's value: `e0 = x + 1`. Range: e_larger in [0, 254] (255 only when sp, which is don't-care)
  and n in [0, 31], so x is in [-31, 254] and fits in 9 signed bits.
- `fp_add_s3`:
  - `n.e = 9'(q.e) - 9'(nz.n);` (zero-extend q.e to 9 bits; a mod-512 subtract gives the right
    signed value).
  - Cancellation: `if (q.sub && !nz.y[27] && !q.sp)` in place of `q.sum == 0`. Compute `nz`
    before the test. Everything else stays as it is.
- `fp_add_s4`: work on `x = n.e` (signed 9-bit), with every condition written against e0 = x + 1:
  - overflow: `x >= 9'sd254 || (x == 9'sd253 && c)` (was `e0 >= 255 || (e0 == 254 && c)`)
  - underflow: `x < -9'sd1 || (x == -9'sd1 && !c)` (was `e0 < 0 || (e0 == 0 && !c)`)
  - exponent out: `8'(x) + {6'd0, c, ~c}`, which is `8'(x + 1 + c) = 8'(e0) + 8'(c)`. This is
    still a 2-operand 8-bit add with the late `c`, the same cost and depth as today's `+ 8'(c)`.
  - Update the comments (s3's normalize comment: "which the +1 folded into s4's constants
    absorbs", in place of "the pre-incremented q.e absorbs").

Why the results stay bit-identical:

- **Exponent path.** x is today's e0 minus 1, identically on every non-special path. Each s4 test
  and the output exponent above is today's expression with e0 replaced by x + 1. Both widths hold
  the full range without wrapping: today's e0 is in [-30, 255], and x is in [-31, 254].
- **0 + 0 add.** Today mn = 0 and e0 = 1 - 31 = -30 < 0. Now x = 0 - 31 = -31 < -1. Both flush
  to `{sa, 0}`, so the -0 of (-0) + (-0) is kept.
- **Cancellation.** `!nz.y[27] <=> q.sum == 0` for any 28-bit sum, as argued above. m == 0 gives
  y == 0, and a nonzero m ends normalized with y[27] = 1. mn, n and sv are unchanged.
- fp_add, fp_sub and the composite functions (exp2, recip, rsqrt, log2) chain s1..s4, so they
  keep the same results. No other RTL uses the fadd stage structs (only otpu_fpipe's otpu_fadd).
- Latency, ports and otpu_fmul are unchanged.

## Expected

Per otpu_fadd:

| Item | LUT | FF |
|---|---|---|
| s2 incrementer removed | -8 | 0 |
| s3 28-bit zero detect removed | -5 to -6 | 0 |
| 9-bit s3.e (subtract, s3.e FF, s4 compares) | -1 to -2 | -1 |
| s4 `+{c,~c}` in place of `+c` | about 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **about -14 to -16** | **-1** |

- **Unit:** about -900 to -1000 LUT and -64 FF, so area_eq falls by about 930 to 1060. That is
  **-2.2% to -2.5%**, comfortably past the -1% gate. Even the incrementer alone (-512) would
  clear it.
- **DSP / BRAM / LUTRAM:** unchanged. otpu_fmul is untouched.
- **fmax:** unchanged or slightly better; 223.4 MHz is expected to hold.
  - The worst path (s2.sum -> norm28 -> e subtract -> s3.e) keeps its structure and gets one bit
    shorter.
  - The `sum == 0` tree no longer loads the s2.sum nets. s2.sum is where all 30 listed worst fadd
    paths start, and those paths are 75% routing, so the lighter load may help.
  - The new sp logic sits at mn[26]'s depth, which is below the e path's.

## Risks

- **Vivado may not collapse `q.sub & !nz.y[27]` into one LUT on the stage-4 outputs.** It could
  instead take the post-mux y[27], one LUT later. The sp path then gets about 0.3 ns longer than
  the mn paths (about 4.4 ns data). That is still close to, but at most level with, the e path's
  4.46 ns.
  - If it becomes the worst path, the fallback is to write `n.sp` from norm28's stage-4 bits:
    have norm28 also return `nz = y4[27] | y4[26]`. That is the same logic, with the level made
    explicit.
- **Off-by-one in the s4 constants** is the main correctness risk. Every one is derived
  mechanically from e0 = x + 1, and the bit-exact RTL tests against the ISS cover overflow,
  underflow and rounding carry-out.
- The `+{6'd0, c, ~c}` form must not be synthesised as a 3-operand add. It is a plain 2-operand
  add, so it shouldn't be.
- **Signed/width pitfalls.**
  - Compare x against sized signed literals (`9'sd254`, `-9'sd1`).
  - Keep `9'(q.e)` a zero-extension of the unsigned 8-bit field.
  - Verilator lint should flag any width mismatch.
implementation:
# fadd: drop the s2 exponent pre-increment and the s3 zero detector

Changed rtl/vpu/otpu_fp.sv only (otpu_fpipe.sv untouched, as the hypothesis says):
- `fp_add_s2`: `q.e = r.e` (no `+ 8'd1`); `fadd_p2_t.e` comment updated.
- `fadd_nm_t.e` is now `signed [8:0]` and holds x = e0 - 1 (range [-31, 254] unless sp).
- `fp_add_s3`: norm28 runs first; cancellation is `q.sub && !nz.y[27] && !q.sp` (norm28 moves any
  nonzero sum up to y[27], so `!y[27] == (sum == 0)`); `n.e = 9'(q.e) - 9'(nz.n)`.
- `fp_add_s4`: tests on x with e0 = x + 1: overflow `x >= 254 || (x == 253 && c)`, underflow
  `x < -1 || (x == -1 && !c)`, exponent `8'(x) + {6'd0, c, ~c}` (= 8'(e0) + 8'(c)).
Checked: the full-design Verilator lint (no otpu_fp warnings), tests/test_fp.py (RTL vs the bit-exact
model, 2 passed), and test_mlp_rtl[1] passed. I built a 40M-vector old-vs-new fp_add equivalence bench
but could not run it here, because running the binary needed approval. No Vivado run.
